preamble: The voiced retroflex stop [ɖ] can lenite to a rhotic when the closure weakens into a trill and the place shifts forward. The clearest case is Romani, which rhoticized Middle Indo-Aryan retroflex stops (ḍ, ṭ, ḍḍ, ṭṭ, ḍh) during or after the Early Romani period; each dialect selected one non-retroflex counterpart, and many chose plain /r/ directly, while conservative dialects keep a distinct ř (phonetically uvular [ʀ] or long [rː]) and others have /l/, /n/ or /d/. Thus Prakrit ḍōmba, the name of a caste of travelling musicians, became Romani rom/rrom 'Romani man', and *maṇḍa became manro/manřo 'bread'. Other Indo-Aryan languages instead keep the retroflex place, giving an intervocalic flap [ɽ].

examples.from: Prakrit ḍōmba (Sanskrit ḍomba) 'member of a caste of travelling musicians'
examples.note: Dialects that selected plain /r/ have rom; conservative Vlax dialects have řom with uvular [ʀ] or long [rː], and some dialects have lom.
The retroflex stop after the nasal became the rhotic; other dialects have mando or manlo.

sources: ROMANI Project, University of Manchester (2022). The structure of Romani: Sound system. https://www.kratylos.org/~raphael/romani/whatis/structure/sound.html
Matras, Y. (2002). Romani: A Linguistic Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511486791
